headline: Public hearing on a National Grid pole at Bridge and Flint streets, plus a proposed unattended-property ordinance and Cleveland Street parking changes.
summary: The agenda includes a public hearing on a National Grid utility pole. It also includes a proposed ordinance on unattended property on public land and a resolution asking the state to do more on homelessness and mental health care.

An Ordinance to amend the Ordinance relative to Chapter 24, Offenses and 
Miscellaneous Provisions, relative to unattended property on public property. 
  
Be it ordained by the City Council of the City of Salem, as follows: 
  
SECTION 1. Chapter 24 is hereby amended by adding the following new section: 
“Sec. 24-33. – Unattended property on public property. 
(a) Prohibited. No person shall store or leave property in or upon any public 
property, sidewalk, or right-of-way for a continuous period exceeding two hours 
when the owner or person responsible for the property is not present. 
(b) Exceptions. This section shall not apply to: 
(1) Property placed or maintained under a permit, license, or other 
authorization issued by the city; 
(2) Bicycles, scooters, strollers, and similar devices that are lawfully parked; 
(3) Trash, recycling, and other items placed for collection in accordance with 
chapter 36; 
(4) Property of the city, any other governmental entity, or a public utility; 
(5) Motor vehicles, trailers, and boats; or 
(6) Campsites and camp materials subject to section 24-31, which shall be 
governed by that section. 
(c) Notice and removal. The city may post a notice on property left in violation of this 
section stating the date and time of the notice, that the property will be removed if it 
is not taken within 24 hours, and where it may be claimed. The city may remove 
property that has not been taken by then. 
(d) Immediate removal. The city may remove property immediately if it poses a 
threat to public health or safety or blocks a sidewalk, entrance, fire hydrant, or 
emergency access, and shall post a notice at the location stating how to claim it. 
(e) Storage and disposal. Removed trash, spoiled food, and items that are soiled, 
infested, or otherwise hazardous may be disposed of immediately. All other removed

police and returned to anyone who reasonably describes it. The City shall not be

(f) Severability. If any provision of this section is held to be invalid by a court of

shall remain in full force and effect.” 
SECTION 2. 
This ordinance shall take effect as provided by City Charter.

MOTIONS, ORDERS AND RESOLUTIONS 
RESOLUTION CALLING UPON THE COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS TO 
ASSUME GREATER RESPONSIBILITY FOR HOMELESSNESS, MENTAL HEALTH 
TREATMENT, AND EQUITABLE MUNICIPAL PARTICIPATION 
WHEREAS, homelessness, serious mental illness, and the lack of adequate treatment facilities and supportive housing 
have become increasingly significant challenges for municipalities throughout the Commonwealth of Massachusetts; and 
WHEREAS, the closure of numerous state-operated psychiatric hospitals, including Danvers State Hospital in 1992, 
fundamentally changed the delivery of mental health services, without the development of sufficient community-based 
treatment and long-term residential care capacity to meet the needs of all vulnerable individuals; and 
WHEREAS, individuals suffering from serious mental illness, particularly those unable to adequately care for themselves, 
deserve access to appropriate medical treatment, supervision, and safe residential facilities rather than being left without 
necessary care; and
7

October 22, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
WHEREAS, municipal police officers and emergency responders are increasingly called upon to manage homelessness-
related incidents and mental health crises, despite lacking the specialized resources, facilities, and authority necessary to 
provide comprehensive psychiatric treatment and long-term care; and 
WHEREAS, although Massachusetts law provides certain emergency psychiatric evaluation and hospitalization 
procedures, there remains a need for more effective access to treatment facilities, appropriate residential placement, and 
continuity of care for individuals requiring ongoing assistance; and 
WHEREAS, municipalities such as the City of Salem, which maintain emergency shelters and provide essential services 
to individuals experiencing homelessness, frequently serve populations extending well beyond their municipal boundaries; 
and 
WHEREAS, the responsibility for providing shelter, supportive services, emergency responses, and related municipal 
resources falls disproportionately upon a limited number of communities, creating an inequitable financial and operational 
burden upon those municipalities and their taxpayers; and 
WHEREAS, homelessness is a regional and statewide challenge that demands meaningful participation from all 351 cities 
and towns within the Commonwealth, rather than relying primarily upon those municipalities willing to provide shelter and 
services; and 
WHEREAS, the City of Salem recognizes both its obligation to protect public health and safety and its responsibility to 
treat individuals experiencing homelessness with dignity, compassion, and respect; 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Salem City Council respectfully but firmly calls upon the Governor of the 
Commonwealth of Massachusetts and the Massachusetts General Court to take the following actions: 
1. EXPAND STATE-SUPPORTED MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT FACILITIES 
Establish, expand, and adequately fund appropriate psychiatric treatment facilities and residential care programs, 
including long-term therapeutic treatment for individuals suffering from serious mental illness who require ongoing 
professional supervision and cannot safely or independently care for themselves. 
2. ESTABLISH AN EFFECTIVE PATHWAY FROM LAW ENFORCEMENT TO TREATMENT 
Develop a clear, timely, and legally appropriate process through which law enforcement officers and emergency 
responders may refer individuals experiencing serious psychiatric crises for professional evaluation, treatment, and, when 
clinically necessary and legally authorized, placement in appropriate state-supported facilities, with full protection of 
individual civil rights and due process. 
3. REQUIRE EQUITABLE PARTICIPATION BY ALL MASSACHUSETTS MUNICIPALITIES 
Enact legislation establishing a mandatory statewide system requiring all 351 cities and towns to contribute meaningfully 
toward addressing homelessness through one or more of the following: 
• Operating or supporting emergency shelters, transitional housing, or permanent supportive housingwithin their 
municipalities. 
• Participating in and financially supporting regional shelter and homelessness assistance programs. 
• Making an annual financial contribution to a state-administered or regional homelessness assistancefund, 
based upon a fair formula considering municipal population, financial capacity, and existing services.
8

October 22, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
 
4. PROVIDE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO MUNICIPALITIES HOSTING SHELTERS 
Establish a dedicated state funding mechanism to ensure that municipalities such as Salem, which maintain shelters and 
provide essential services to individuals from surrounding communities, receive equitable financial assistance reflecting 
the regional demands placed upon their public safety departments, emergency services, infrastructure, and taxpayers. 
5. ESTABLISH STATEWIDE ACCOUNTABILITY AND COORDINATION 
Develop a comprehensive statewide strategy establishing clear standards for municipal participation, regional 
coordination, treatment availability, supportive housing, and accountability, ensuring that no individual community is left to 
shoulder a disproportionate share of these responsibilities. 
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Salem City Council recognizes that homelessness, particularly when complicated 
by serious mental illness, cannot be adequately addressed through municipal ordinances, police intervention, emergency 
shelters, or local resources alone, and that lasting solutions require sustained leadership, financial commitment, and 
direct action by the Commonwealth. 
BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED, that copies of this resolution be transmitted to Governor Maura Healey, the President of the 
Massachusetts Senate, the Speaker of the Massachusetts House of Representatives, the Secretary of Health and Human 
Services, and the members of Salem's legislative delegation, urging their consideration and legislative action.

ORDERED: That an Ad Hoc Committee of the Salem City Council be established for the 
purpose of studying and developing a proposed redesign of the official City Seal and 
preparing proposed amendments to the City of Salem Code of Ordinances necessary to 
effectuate and implement any new City Seal adopted by the City Council. 
BE IT FURTHER ORDERED: That the Ad Hoc Committee shall: 
1. Review the existing City Seal, including its historical origins, evolution, current 
design, symbolism, and the existing legal description contained in Section 2-1 of the 
City of Salem Code of Ordinances; 
2. Review the findings and recommendations of the Salem City Seal Task Force 
submitted on submitted November 10, 2025; 
3. Develop one or more proposed designs for a revised official City Seal that reflect 
Salem's history, identity, values, and contemporary community, while considering 
the appropriate distinction between the official City Seal and other City branding or 
departmental logos;

4. Provide meaningful opportunities for public input concerning any proposed redesign, 
including consideration of public forums, presentations, surveys, or other appropriate 
methods of community engagement; 
5. Consult with appropriate City officials, departments, boards, commissions, historical 
organizations, design professionals, historians, legal counsel, and other persons or 
organizations as the Committee determines appropriate; 
6. Determine the appropriate legal description of the proposed new City Seal, including 
the visual elements, wording, dates, inscriptions, motto, and other features that 
should be incorporated into the City's Code of Ordinances; 
7. Prepare proposed amendments to Section 2-1 of the City of Salem Code of 
Ordinances, or such other provisions of the Code as may be necessary, to replace 
the existing legal description of the City Seal with the description of the proposed 
new Seal; 
8. Consider and recommend appropriate provisions concerning the use of the official 
City Seal, including, as appropriate, provisions distinguishing the official City Seal 
from City logos, branding, and other identifying marks; 
9. Develop recommendations concerning implementation and transition, including the 
appropriate date for implementation of a new Seal and the treatment of existing 
official documents, records, signage, vehicles, equipment, publications, electronic 
materials, and other City property bearing the existing Seal; 
10. Consult with the City Solicitor and City Clerk concerning the legal requirements for 
adoption, authentication, custody, reproduction, and use of the official City Seal and 
concerning the proposed amendments to the Code of Ordinances; and 
11. Submit a final report and recommendations to the full City Council, including a 
recommended design for the revised City Seal and proposed ordinance language 
necessary to amend the City's Code of Ordinances. 
BE IT FURTHER ORDERED: That the Ad Hoc Committee shall consist of five members, 
three members of the City Council, to be appointed by the President of the City Council in 
accordance with the Rules of the City Council, one of whom shall be designated Chair by 
the President, and two additional members, the city solicitor or their designee and the city 
clerk or their designee.  
BE IT FURTHER ORDERED: That the Ad Hoc Committee shall report its 
recommendations to the City Council no later than May 27, 2027, unless an extension is 
authorized by the City Council. 
BE IT FURTHER ORDERED: That upon completion of its report and recommendations, 
the Ad Hoc Committee shall be dissolved, unless otherwise ordered by the City Council.

Councillor Varela offered the following report on the Committee on Ordinances, Licenses 
and Legal Affairs to whom the matter was referred the matter Discuss Language of a Light 
Shield Ordinance. 
 
Has Considered said matter and would recommend: Sec. 24-33 Light Shield Ordinance 
No outdoor floodlighting or decorative lighting, except lighting primarily designed to 
illuminate walks, driveways, outdoor living areas, or outdoor recreational facilities, or 
temporary holiday lighting in use for not longer than a eight-week period in any calendar 
year, shall be permitted. Any permanent lighting permitted by the preceding sentence shall 
be continuous, indirect, and installed in a manner that will prevent direct light from shining 
onto any street or abutting property. All municipal lighting shall be exempt from the 
provisions of this ordinance. The Building Inspector, or their designee, shall enforce this 
division. 
Penalties. 
Whoever violates any provision of this article shall be subject to a fine of $25.00 for the first 
offense and $25.00 for any subsequent offense.
